source.market_name: Will OpenAI’s market cap be between $1.25T and $1.5T at market close on IPO day?

market_name: Will OpenAI’s market cap be between $1.25T and $1.5T at market close on IPO day?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any credible IPO-timing or valuation headline coincides with the probability move; without a catalyst treat as noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT move vs QQQ/mega-cap tech beta to see if any move is idiosyncratic or just market beta.
time_plan.2h: Look for confirmation across NVDA and other AI-exposed names; a lone MSFT move without breadth argues against a real OpenAI signal.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether bracket probability shift persisted or mean-reverted; bracket markets are prone to thin-liquidity noise.
time_plan.12h: Close out research view; record whether MSFT diverged from index and whether any public OpenAI IPO news emerged.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft holds a large economic stake in OpenAI, so a credible public valuation for OpenAI is the most direct listed-market read-through. However, this market asks about a NARROW valuation bracket ($1.25T-$1.5T) on a hypothetical IPO day, not whether OpenAI IPOs or at what headline value. A move in the implied probability of hitting this specific bracket carries almost no clean directional information for MSFT: probability could rise because valuation expectations converge downward into the band or upward into it, and the dominant unresolved node is whether any IPO happens at all by end-2026. The signal-to-noise here is very poor.

evidence_used: Market question concerns a narrow $1.25T-$1.5T market-cap bracket for a hypothetical OpenAI first-day close
Resolution allows 'No IPO by December 31, 2026' — the base case is heavy conditionality on an event that has not been scheduled
Microsoft is OpenAI's largest strategic/economic partner and the most liquid listed proxy for OpenAI valuation
No IPO is currently announced; OpenAI remains private
uncertainty_notes: The market is a narrow bracket, so probability moves do not map to a directional valuation view
The dominant uncertainty is IPO occurrence/timing, not the exact bracket
OpenAI is private; no direct tradable instrument exists, and proxy exposure (MSFT) is diluted by its own massive standalone business
Polymarket bracket liquidity can be thin, generating spurious probability swings

llm_justification.summary: This market maps very weakly to public markets. It concerns a narrow valuation bracket for a not-yet-announced OpenAI IPO, so implied-probability moves carry little clean directional signal. The closest liquid proxy is Microsoft via its OpenAI stake, but the read-through is diluted and ambiguous. We assign unclear direction and low confidence, well below the 700bps tradable threshold.
key_assumptions: Microsoft remains the most exposed liquid listed proxy to OpenAI valuation
A bracket-probability move does not encode whether valuation is rising or falling
No concrete IPO announcement is imminent within the 12h window
failure_modes: A genuine IPO-timing or valuation headline could move MSFT/NVDA far more than this bracket market predicts, decoupling the proxy from the signal
The probability move may be pure thin-market noise with no informational content
MSFT's standalone fundamentals dominate its price, swamping any OpenAI read-through
Information could already be public, making the market lagging rather than leading
Bracket resolution mechanics (higher bracket on ties, abbreviated sessions) add noise unrelated to any asset move
